finding: Decomposing directed information flow into synergy vs redundancy (conditional interaction information) shows that NO component tracks faithful IIT4 big-Phi: synergy is orthogonal to Phi (Pearson r=0.030; ECA parity has redundancy=0 throughout). The decisive evidence is a DOUBLE dissociation: rule 60 has the highest Phi (13.6) yet zero synergy (next=self XOR left = pure UNIQUE information from one source), while rule 90 has maximal synergy (4.0) yet Phi=0 (neighbour XOR but the system is reducible). So synergy is neither necessary (rule 60 counterexample) nor sufficient (rule 90 counterexample) for integration. This extends H_293 (no ORDER of TE equals Phi) one level deeper: no COMPONENT of flow equals Phi either. Integration is a system-cut (whole-vs-parts) property that does not reduce to any local information-flow decomposition. Rule 90 over-predicts under LZ (H_288), multivariate TE (H_293), AND synergy (here) — the apex of the cross-measure 'local flow/complexity present, global integration absent' signature. Maximally strengthens the paper's thesis.
honest_limits: L1: conditional interaction information (co-information) is the 2-source NET synergy/redundancy summary, NOT the full Williams-Beer 4-atom PID (which would separate rule 60's unique term explicitly); net-level conclusion already decisive.
L2: ECA parity family has redundancy=0 (sources do not share target info); redundancy-vs-Phi needs a redundancy>0 substrate (copy/majority).
L3: II_c is self-conditioned (consistent with H_293); unconditioned/multi-lag differ.
L4: n=4 small, 10-rule panel — direction (synergy perp Phi, double dissociation) robust, exact r panel-dependent.
L5: ECA = flow proxy, not phenomenal claim.
L6: structure-cut big-Phi; absence-of-correlation robust to scale offset.
L7: verdict is a toy-substrate measurement fact.
